items.title: [FDD Diary #25] The Trap After the Spec
content:
Had the spec. Had the process. Had the tests.
Built six features at once.

All six blew up at once.

File sync hit remote commands.
GPU tangled with monitoring.
Alerts had nothing to connect to.

A spec is a map.
Can't walk every road at the same time.

What should I build first?
Everything's important.

Went back to the beginning.
What did I want?
Send a job from laptop to desktop. Get the result back.
That's it.

GPU sharing? Later.
Auto-recovery? Later.

'Start small.'
Heard it a hundred times.
Nobody says what 'small' means.

Fewest features? No.

Smallest = the moment the experience I wanted happens once.

Ten features, no experience? Nothing.
One feature, that experience? Beginning.

items.title: [FDD Diary #26] The Cafe Test
content:
Opened my laptop at the cafe.
Needed a file from home.
Not there.

Shit.

That moment.
Eliminating that moment.
That's the whole product.

Spec says 'file sync.'
UX says 'open it at the cafe, it's there.'

Build from the system side:
'Sync success: 1,247 files. 3 conflicts.'
Feature works. Infuriating.

Build from the human side:
Open laptop. File's there. Done.

Spec can be right and UX can still be wrong.

Never read a line of code in my life.
But experience review?

'Opened at the cafe. File there?'
There? Pass. Not there? Fail.

Answered 'is this what I wanted?' without touching the code.

That's the weapon.

items.title: [FDD Diary #27] AI Gives You Boundaries
content:
'SSH?' 'Yes. Not behind NAT.'
'Port forwarding?' 'Yes. Security risk.'
'VPN?' 'Yes. Slow.'
'QUIC?' 'Yes. Blocked on some networks.'

Twenty rounds of ping-pong.

AI doesn't give you the answer.
It gives you a boundary.

Every boundary turned out to be a requirement.

Twenty rounds. Chat gets long.
Most people open a new chat.
Start from scratch.

Wrong.

The conversation is the research.
The fight is the data.
Don't throw it away.

New chat — AI is a new hire.
Same chat with context — AI is a colleague.
Same AI. Different context.

Conversation history = research data.
'Won't work' = requirement.
Twenty rounds = twenty boundaries = twenty spec conditions.

Don't throw it away.
Don't open a new chat.
Take the fight records and go back.
